source.title: DLM-Scope: Mechanistic Interpretability of Diffusion Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Xu Wang; Bin Jiang; Yunyang Wan; Bao-Song Yang; Lingpeng Kong; Di-Fan Zou

record.tranche_reason: The study scores SAE-feature explanations by asking a judge model to predict activation on unmarked examples. This conceptually tests explanation predictiveness, but it does not audit neuron poles or use the Qwen3-32B pole-counting method.
record.gate_note: The relevant reported results are four individual auto-interpretation accuracy scores in Appendix E. The paper describes the scoring protocol and provides examples, but reports no aggregate score distribution or share of features above a defined threshold. Other SAE, steering, decoding-order, and transfer results do not bear on the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on diffusion LMs (Dream-7B, LLaDA-8B). It uses the simulation-style auto-interpretation protocol only as a tool to show its own SAE latents are interpretable. The scored units are SAE latents, not the model's own neurons or neuron poles, so they are a different construct from what V1–V7 name. Only a handful of hand-picked examples are scored. The paper says up to 1000 latents were scored per SAE, but it reports no aggregate, share or threshold. It therefore gives no result on how often neuron explanations predict activations.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that DLM-trained SAEs are a practical interpretability interface, with good sparsity-fidelity trade-offs and some early-layer loss reduction. They say the features are human-interpretable and validated by auto-interpretation scores. They draw no conclusions about neurons or about the population share of well-explained units.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates Dream-7B SAE latent explanations using an automated prediction-accuracy protocol; it does not reproduce the Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit.
record.method_sensitivity: The interpretation score uses gpt-4o-mini; no comparison across judges is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Auto-interpretation accuracies for selected Dream-7B SAE latents: 1.00, 0.714, 0.929 and 0.286 (Appendix E). Figure 1 also shows scores of 0.85 (L5-527), 0.90 (L14-520) and 0.31 (L23-615).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In diffusion LMs, the explanations of some SAE latents predict held-out activations well and others poorly, under simulation-style scoring with a gpt-4o-mini judge.

record.problems: Only four selected SAE-feature examples have reported scores; the paper gives no aggregate distribution, defined threshold for a good score, or uncertainty estimates. The scored objects are Dream-7B SAE features, not audited neuron poles, and only one judge model is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly score explanations on new examples. Qualitative feature descriptions without a reported score were not entered as rows.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or share estimates.
No neuron-level job shares across models or scales.
No vision models and no test of the cat-and-car neuron or recursive generalization.
No comparison of architectures, regularization or tools on neuron interpretability share.
No attribution graphs built from neurons.
Neuron explanations are never checked against held-out firing; only SAE latents are scored, as examples.
No population share of well-scored neurons, no threshold, and no comparison of explainer models (a single gpt-4o-mini judge).

record.verdict_notes: Figure 1 lists three further interpretability scores (0.85, 0.90, 0.31) that the record omits. If these SAE-latent results are kept, add them under fits_no_version; they bear on no version. The paper says up to 1000 latents per SAE were scored but gives no aggregate. The reader's labels on V6 were wrong: the rows concern SAE latents and are illustrative examples, so no verdict is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or estimates of one-job, two-job, or not-understood shares.
No cross-model or scale comparison of neuron-pole job shares, and no models approaching trillions of parameters.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No test of architecture, regularization, or tool quality as explanations for interpretable-neuron shares.
No attribution-graph test of whether a model's own neurons suffice as circuit units.
The paper scores explanations from Dream-7B SAE features on unmarked examples, but does not estimate how often inspected explanations fail across a representative population of neurons or poles.

The paper reports automated scores for four selected Dream-7B SAE features, but not the population share scoring well, a defined good-score threshold, or a comparison across stronger explainer models.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The reported accuracy of 0.286 shows that this feature's explanation predicted activation poorly on the scoring examples (r4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: These selected features had reported scores of 1.00, 0.714, and 0.929, respectively, so the low-score result does not hold for every illustrated feature (r1, r2, r3).
